title: Sumsets and additive combinatorics
summary: The study of $A+B = \{a+b\}$ for finite sets. Small doubling $|A+A| \le K|A|$ forces structure (Freiman), and Fourier analysis on $\mathbb Z/N$ measures how random a set is.
key_statements: |A+A| \le K|A| \Rightarrow A \subset \text{a generalised progression of size } O_K(|A|)

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #331
research_problems.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for all large $N$$$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg
N^{1/2}$$and$$\lvert B\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg N^{1/2}.$$
Is it true that there are infinitely many solutions to $a_1-a_2=b_1-b_2\neq 0$ with $a_1,a_2\in A$
and $b_1,b_2\in B$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #138
research_problems.statement:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #36
research_problems.statement: Find the value of the limit of `MinOverlapQuotient`!

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1199
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #142
research_problems.statement:
Prove an asymptotic formula for $r_k(N)$, the largest possible size of a subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ that does not contain any non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.
That is, find $f_k$ with $r_k(N) / f_k(N) \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #763
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Can there exist some constant $c>0$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+O(1)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #172
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist arbitrarily large finite $A$ such that all sums
and products of distinct elements in $A$ are the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #867
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that if $A=\{a_1<\cdots <a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has no solutions to
$$a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$$
then
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \frac{N}{2}+O(1)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #840
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest quasi-Sidon subset $A\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$, where we say
that $A$ is quasi-Sidon if
$$\lvert A+A\rvert=(1+o(1))\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}.$$
How does $f(N)$ grow?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #141
research_problems.statement: Let $k≥3$. Are there $k$ consecutive primes in arithmetic progression?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #785
research_problems.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets of positive integers such that $A+B$ contains all
large integers. Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #198
research_problems.statement:
The answer is no; Erdős and Graham report this was proved by Baumgartner, presumably referring to
the paper [Ba75], which does not state this exactly, but the following simple construction is
implicit in [Ba75].

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #186
research_problems.statement:
Let $F(N)$ be the maximal size of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ which is 'non-averaging', so that
no $n\in A$ is the arithmetic mean of at least two elements in $A$. What is the order of growth
of $F(N)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1097
research_problems.statement:
The main conjecture: for any finite set of integers $A$ with $|A| = n$, the number of distinct
common differences in three-term arithmetic progressions is $O(n^{3/2})$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #864
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set such that there exists at most one $n$ with more than one
solution to $n=a+b$ (with $a\leq b\in A$). Estimate the maximal possible size of $|A|$. In
particular, is it true that
$$|A| \leq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} N^{1/2}?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #781
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $n$ such that any $2$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ contains a
monochromatic $k$-term descending wave: a sequence $x_1<\cdots <x_k$ such that, for $1<j<k$,
$$x_j \geq \frac{x_{j+1}+x_{j-1}}{2}.$$
Estimate $f(k)$.

(b) Is it true that $f(k)=k^2-k+1$ for all $k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #966
research_problems.statement:
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1187
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, in any finite colouring of the integers, there are monochromatic
arithmetic progressions of primes of length $k$?

(b) Let $k\geq 3$. In any finite colouring of the integers, are there monochromatic arithmetic
progressions of length $k$ whose common difference is a prime?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #328
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and $C>0$ is such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\leq C$ for all
$n\in\mathbb{N}$. Can $A$ be partitioned into $t$ many subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_t$ (where
$t=t(C)$ depends only on $C$) such that $1_{A_i}\ast 1_{A_i}(n)<C$ for all $1\leq i\leq t$
and $n\in \mathbb{N}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #53
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that, for every $k$, if $\lvert A\rvert$ is
sufficiently large depending on $k$, then there are least $\lvert A\rvert^k$ many integers which
are either the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #272
research_problems.statement:
Let $N \in\mathbb{N}$. We say that $\{A_1, ..., A_t\}\subseteq
\mathcal{P}(\{1, \dots, N\})$ is an arithmetic intersection set if
$A_i \cap A_j$ is a non-empty arithmetic progression for each $i \neq j$.

For each $N > 0$, let $t$ be the largest size of an arithmetic
intersection set.

Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #245
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 3?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #806
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$. Must there exist some
$B\subset\mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert B\rvert=o(n^{1/2})$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #772
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $k\geq 1$ and $H_k(n)$ be the maximal $r$ such that if $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ has
$\lvert A\rvert=n$ and $\| 1_A\ast 1_A\|_\infty \leq k$ then $A$ contains a Sidon set of size at
least $r$.

Is it true that $H_k(n)/n^{1/2}\to \infty$?

(b) Is it true that $H_k(n) > n^{1/2+c}$ for some constant $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #41
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that the triple sums $a+b+c$ are all distinct
for $a,b,c \in A$ (aside from the trivial coincidences). Is it true that
$$\liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{\lvert A \cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/3}}=0?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #865
research_problems.statement:
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all large $N$, if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\frac{5}{8}N+C$ then there are distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that $a+b,a+c,b+c\in A$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #43
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible size of a Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

(a) If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

(b) If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #818
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers such that $\lvert A+A\rvert \ll \lvert A\rvert$. Is it true that
$$\lvert AA\rvert \gg \frac{\lvert A\rvert^2}{(\log \lvert A\rvert)^C}$$
for some constant $C>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #707
research_problems.statement:
It is false that any finite Sidon set can be embedded in a perfect
different set modulo some $n$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #44
research_problems.statement:
Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #895
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, if $G$ is a triangle-free graph on
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ then there must exist three independent points $a,b,a+b$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1193
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the lower density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $0$?

(b) Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ and let $g(n)$ be a non-decreasing function of $n$ which is always $>0$.

Is the upper density of
$$\{ n : 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=g(n)\}$$
always $<c$ for some constant $c<1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #139
research_problems.statement:
Let $r_k(N)$ be the size of the largest subset of ${1,...,N}$ which does not contain a non-trivial
$k$-term arithmetic progression. Prove that $r_k(N) = o(N)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #749
research_problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #350
research_problems.statement:
If `A ⊂ ℕ` is a finite set of integers all of whose subset sums are distinct then `∑ n ∈ A, 1/n < 2`.
Proved by Ryavec.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #30
research_problems.statement:
Let $h(N)$ be the maximum size of a Sidon set in $\{1, \dots, N\}$.

Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varepsilon}(N^\varepsilon)$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #645
research_problems.statement:
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1186
research_problems.statement:
Let $\delta_k$ be such that in any $2$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there exist at least
$(\delta_k+o(1))n^2$ many monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progressions. Give reasonable bounds
(or even an asymptotic formula) for $\delta_k$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #819
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(N)$ be maximal such that there exists $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert=\lfloor N^{1/2}\rfloor$ such that $\lvert (A+A)\cap [1,N]\rvert=f(N)$.
Estimate $f(N)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #539
research_problems.statement:
We say that $m$ is a cofactor lower bound for a given $n$ if, for every set $A$ of $n$
non-negative integers, there are at least $m$ cofactors $a / (a, b)$, where $a, b\in A$.

Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that, for any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, the
set$$\left\{ \frac{a}{(a,b)}: a,b\in A\right\}$$has size at least $h(n)$. Estimate $h(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #741
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive upper density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive upper density?

(b) Is there a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that if $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ then $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
cannot both have bounded gaps?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1
research_problems.statement:
A finite set of naturals $A$ is said to be a sum-distinct set for $N \in \mathbb{N}$ if
$A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ and the sums $\sum_{a\in S}a$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq A$

If $A\subseteq\{1, ..., N\}$ with $|A| = n$ is such that the subset sums $\sum_{a\in S}a$ are
distinct for all $S\subseteq A$ then
$$
  N \gg 2 ^ n.
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #847
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon > 0$ such that
in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no
three-term arithmetic progression.

Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic
progression?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #764
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Can there exist some constant $c>0$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq N} 1_A\ast 1_A\ast 1_A(n) = cN+O(1)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #877
research_problems.statement:
Let $f_m(n)$ count the number of maximal sum-free subsets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ - that is,
there are no solutions to $a=b+c$ in $A$ and $A$ is maximal with this property. Estimate $f(n)$
- is it true that $f_m(n)=o(2^{n/2})$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #789
research_problems.statement:
Given a non-negative integer $n$, we say $m$ is a separating cardinality of
subset sums if, for any set $A$ of $n$ integers, there is some $B\subseteq A$ of
size $\geq m$ such that subset sums of $B$ can only ever coincide when the
subsets have the same cardinality.

Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$
then there is $B\subseteq A$ with $\lvert B\rvert \geq h(n)$ such that if
$a_1+\cdots+a_r=b_1+\cdots+b_s$ with $a_i,b_i\in B$ then $r=s$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #484
research_problems.statement:
Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is
$k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many
integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$
where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #171
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ and integer $t\geq 1$, if $N$ is sufficiently large and
$A$ is a subset of $[t]^N$ of size at least $\epsilon t^N$ then $A$ must contain a combinatorial
line $P$ (a set $P=\{p_1,\ldots,p_t\}$ where for each coordinate $1\leq j\leq t$ the $j$th
coordinate of $p_i$ is either $i$ or constant).

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1145
research_problems.statement:
Let $A=\{1\leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$ and $B=\{1\leq b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ be sets of integers with
$a_n/b_n\to 1$.

If $A+B$ contains all sufficiently large positive integers then is it true that
$\limsup 1_A\ast 1_B(n)=\infty$?

Formalization note: There's some discussion in the comments of [erdosproblems.com/28] and
[erdosproblems.com/1145] about whether or not $0$ should be included in $A$ or $B$ and has been
left purposely ambiguous. Problem 1145 was originally written as $A + B = \mathbb{N}$, which
would imply that $0$ would need to exist in $A$ or $B$ to include $1$ in $A + B$. However,

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #340
research_problems.statement:
Let $A = \{1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 21, 31, 45, 66, 81, 97, \ldots\}$ be the greedy Sidon sequence:
we begin with $1$ and iteratively include the next smallest integer that preserves the
Sidon property (i.e. there are no non-trivial solutions to $a + b = c + d$). What is the
order of growth of $A$? Is it true that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| \gg N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$ and large $N$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1179
research_problems.statement:
Let $0<\epsilon<1$ and let $g_\epsilon(N)$ be the minimal $k$ such that if $G$ is an abelian
group of size $N$ and $A\subseteq G$ is a uniformly random subset of size $k$, and
$$F_A(g) = \#\left\{ S\subseteq A : g = \sum_{x\in S}x\right\},$$
then, with probability $\to 1$ as $N\to \infty$,
$$\left\lvert F_A(g)-\frac{2^k}{N}\right\rvert \leq \epsilon \frac{2^k}{N}$$
for all $g\in G$.

Estimate $g_\epsilon(N)$ - in particular, is it true that for all $\epsilon>0$
$$g_\epsilon(N)=(1+o_\epsilon(1))\log_2N?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #476
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$. Let
$$
A\hat{+}A = \{ a+b : a\neq b \in A\}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
\lvert A\hat{+}A\rvert \geq \min(2\lvert A\rvert-3,p)?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #658
research_problems.statement:
Let $\delta>0$ and $N$ be sufficiently large depending on $\delta$. Is it true that if
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert \geq \delta N^2$ then $A$ must contain the
vertices of a square?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #52
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #483
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $N$ such that if $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured then
there is a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$. Estimate $f(k)$. In particular, is it true
that $f(k) < c^k$ for some constant $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #787
research_problems.statement:
Let $g(n)$ be maximal such that given any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$ there
exists some $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq g(n)$ such that $b_1+b_2\not\in A$ for all
$b_1\neq b_2\in B$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #109
research_problems.statement:
Any $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains a sumset $B+C$ where both $B$ and $C$
are infinite.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #185
research_problems.statement:
Let $f_3(n)$ be the maximal size of a subset of $\{0,1,2\}^n$ which contains no three points on
a line. Is it true that $f_3(n)=o(3^n)$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1198
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{N}$ is $2$-coloured, must there exist an infinite set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ such that
all expressions of the shape
$$\sum_{j=1}^{k}\prod_{i\in S_j}a_i,$$
for $k\geq 1$ and pairwise disjoint nonempty finite sets of indices $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ (excluding the
trivial expressions $a_i$, that is $k=1$ and $|S_1|=1$), have the same colour?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1213
research_problems.statement:
Let $a,K\geq 1$. Does there exist $f(a,K)$ such that if $a=a_1<\cdots <a_s$ is a sequence of
integers with $a_s> f(a,K)$ and with bounded gaps $a_{i+1}-a_i\leq K$ then there are two distinct
intervals $I$ and $J$ such that
$$\sum_{i\in I}a_i=\sum_{j\in J}a_j?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #39
research_problems.statement:
Is there an infinite Sidon set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2-\epsilon}$
for all $\varepsilon > 0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #337
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis (of any finite order) such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert=o(N)$. Is it true that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1192
research_problems.statement:
For $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ let $f_r(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=a_1+\cdots+a_r$
with $a_i\in A$.

Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #42
research_problems.statement:
Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #241
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(N)$ be the maximum size of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that the sums $a+b+c$ with
$a,b,c\in A$ are all distinct (aside from the trivial coincidences).

Formalization note: this is generalized to allow for different $r$.

Is it true that $f(N)\sim N^{1/3}$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #899
research_problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1191
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Is it true that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}=0?$$

(b) Does there exist an infinite Sidon set $A$ such that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^c>0$$
for some $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #14
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?

(b) Is it possible that $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| = o(N^\frac{1}{2})$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #219
research_problems.statement:
Are there arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes?
Solution: yes.
Ref: Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, _The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions_

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #3
research_problems.statement:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #155
research_problems.statement:
Let $F(N)$ be the size of the largest Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.

Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #168
research_problems.statement:
(a) What is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$?

(b) Is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$ irrational?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 1
research_problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ positive integers. Does $A$ contain a sum-free set
of size at least $\frac n 3 + Ω(n)$, where $Ω(n) → ∞$ as $n → ∞$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 2
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ be a set of $n$ integers. Is there a set $S \subset A$ of size
$(\log n)^{100}$ such that the restricted sumset$S \hat{+} S$ is disjoint from $A$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 3
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset [0,1]$ is open and has measure greater than $\frac{1}{3}$. Is there a
solution to $xy = z$ with $x, y, z \in A$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 16
research_problems.statement: What is the largest subset of $[N]$ with no solution to $x + 3y = 2z + 2w$ in distinct integers $x, y, z, w$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 19
research_problems.statement:
What is $C$, the infimum of all exponents $c$ for which the following is true, uniformly for
$0 < \alpha < 1$? Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n \times \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density
$\alpha$. Write $N := 2^n$. Then there is some $d \neq 0$ such that $A$ contains $\gg \alpha^c N^2$
corners $(x,y), (x,y+d), (x+d,y)$.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 24
research_problems.statement:
If $A$ is a set of $n$ integers, what is the maximum number of affine translates of the set
$\lbrace 0,1,3 \rbrace$ that $A$ can contain?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 25
research_problems.statement:
For which values of $k$ is the following true: whenever we partition $[N] = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_k$,
$\left|\bigcup^k_{i=1} (A_i \hat{+} A_i)\right| \geq \frac{1}{10} N$?

For which values of $k$ is the following true: whenever we partition $[N] = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_k$,
$\left|\bigcup^k_{i=1} (A_i \hat{+} A_i)\right| \geq \frac{1}{10} N$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 26
research_problems.statement:
Let $A_1, \dots, A_{100}$ be "cubes" in $\mathbb{F}^n_3$.
Is it true that $A_1 + \dots + A_{100} = \mathbb{F}^n_3$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 27
research_problems.statement:
What is the size of the smallest set $A \subset \mathbb{Z} / p\mathbb{Z}$ (with at least two elements)
for which no element in the sumset $A + A$ has a unique representation?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 28
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 33
research_problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many $q$ for which there is a set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$,
$|A| = (\sqrt{2} + o(1))q^{1/2}$, with $A + A = \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$? [Gr24]

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 35
research_problems.statement:
Lower bound for $c(p)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$, improving the known value $\sqrt{4/7}$ at
$p = 2$ or the known value $0.64$ at $p = \infty$.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 38
research_problems.statement:
Can we improve the lower bound? The answer sequence must be eventually nonnegative, since
`=O` compares norms.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 39
research_problems.statement:
If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is random, $|A| = \sqrt{p}$, can we almost surely cover
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $100\sqrt{p}$ translates of $A$? [Gr24]

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 40
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(r)$ be the smallest constant such that there exists an infinite sequence of $n$'s together
with subspaces $V_n \leq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $V_n + H(r) = \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and
$|V_n| = \left(f(r) + o(1)\right) \frac{2^n}{|H(r)|}$.

Does $f(r) \to \infty$? [Gr24]

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 41
research_problems.statement:
[Ma15] proved that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, finitely many rotations of the pyjama set of width
$\varepsilon$ cover the plane. This implies that the set we are taking the infimum over in `minCopies`
is non-empty.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 42
research_problems.statement: Can the Cohn-Elkies scheme be used to prove the optimal bound for circle-packings in 2 dimensions?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 47
research_problems.statement: Suppose that a large sieve process leaves a set of quadratic size. Is that set quadratic?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 49
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with $|A + A| \leq K|A|$. Is it true that $A$
is covered by $K^{O(1)}$ translates of a subspace of size $\leq |A|$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 50
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 51
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density $\alpha$. What is the largest size of coset
guaranteed to be contained in $2A$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 52
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with an additive complement of size $K$.
Does $2A$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 53
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is partitioned in to sets $A_1, ..., A_K$.
Does $2A_i$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$ for some $i$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 54
research_problems.statement:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$
whenever $|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure
$\gamma_\infty(K) \geq 0.99$. Does the sumset $10K = K + \cdots + K$ ($10$ times) contain a compact
convex set $C$ with $\gamma_\infty(C) \geq 0.01$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 58
research_problems.statement:
Suppose $A, B ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ both have size at least $N^{0.49}$. Must the sumset $A + B$
contain a composite number?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 60
research_problems.statement:
Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, whenever $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is a set of squares
with $|A| ≥ 2$, the sumset $A + A$ satisfies $|A + A| ≥ |A|^{1 + c}$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 61
research_problems.statement: Suppose that $A + A$ contains the first $n$ squares. Is $|A| \geq n^{1 - o(1)}$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 66
research_problems.statement:
Is there always a sum of two squares between $X - \frac{1}{10}X^{1/4}$ and $X$?
We formalize this as an eventual statement for sufficiently large real $X$.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 72
research_problems.statement:
The **no-k-in-line problem**:
For which $k > 2$ does every $N \times N$ grid with $N \geq k$ contain a set of $(k - 1) N$ points
with no $k$ on a line, so that `AllowedSetSize k N` is the pigeonhole bound $(k - 1) N$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 77
research_problems.statement:
Given $n$ points in the unit disc, must there be a triangle of area at most $n^{-2+o(1)}$
determined by them?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 82
research_problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $n$. For how many $\theta \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$
must we have $\sum_{a \in A} \cos(2\pi a\theta) = 0$? The answer is the function `minZeros`.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 85
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 94
research_problems.statement: Let `A ⊂ R` be a set of positive outer measure. Does $A$ contain an affine copy of `{1, 1/2, 1/4, . . . }`?

title: Arithmetic Ramsey theory
summary: Colour the integers with finitely many colours; some colour class contains a given structure. Schur: a monochromatic $x+y=z$. Van der Waerden: arbitrarily long monochromatic progressions. Rado: exactly which linear systems are partition regular.
key_statements: \forall\, r\ \exists\, N:\ [1,N] = C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r \Rightarrow \exists i,\ x,y,z\in C_i,\ x+y=z

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #46
research_problems.statement:
Does every finite colouring of the integers have a monochromatic solution to
$1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$ with $2\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #894
research_problems.statement:
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be a lacunary sequence (so there exists some
$\epsilon>0$ with $n_{k+1}\geq (1+\epsilon)n_k$ for all $k$). Is it true that there must exist a
finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ with no monochromatic solutions to $a-b\in A$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #966
research_problems.statement:
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #645
research_problems.statement:
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #45
research_problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$. Is there an integer $n_k$ such that, if $D=\{ 1<d<n_k : d\mid n_k\}$, then for any
$k$-colouring of $D$ there is a monochromatic subset $D'\subseteq D$ such that
$\sum_{d\in D'}\frac{1}{d}=1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #484
research_problems.statement:
Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is
$k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many
integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$
where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #948
research_problems.statement:
Is there a function $f(n)$ and a $k$ such that in any $k$-colouring of the integers there exists a
sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ such that $a_n < f(n)$ for infinitely many $n$ and the set
$$\left\{ \sum_{i \in S} a_i : \textrm{finite nonempty } S \right\}$$
does not contain all colours?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #483
research_problems.statement:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $N$ such that if $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured then
there is a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$. Estimate $f(k)$. In particular, is it true
that $f(k) < c^k$ for some constant $c>0$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #532
research_problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{N}$ is 2-coloured then is there some infinite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that
all finite subset sums$$ \sum_{n\in S}n$$(as $S$ ranges over all non-empty finite subsets of $A$)
are monochromatic?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 14
research_problems.statement: Is $W(k, r)$ a polynomial in $r$, for fixed $k$?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 21
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $a_1, \dots, a_k$ are integers which do not satisfy Rado's condition: thus if
$\sum_{i \in I} a_i = 0$ then $I = \emptyset$. It then follows from Rado's theorem that the
equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$ is not partition regular. Write $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ for
the least number of colours required in order to colour $\mathbb{N}$ so that there is no
monochromatic solution to $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$. Is $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ bounded in
terms of $k$ only?

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 22
research_problems.statement:
If $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ is $r$-coloured then, for $N \geqslant N_0(r)$, there are integers
$x, y \geqslant 3$ such that $x + y, xy$ have the same colour.

research_problems.title: Green's Problem 23
research_problems.statement:
Suppose that $\mathbb{N}$ is finitely coloured. Are there $x,y$ of the same colour such that $x^2 +
 y^2$ is a square?

title: Discrepancy
summary: How evenly can a $\pm1$ sequence be balanced on a family of sets? Erdős asked whether $\sup_{n,d}|\sum_{k\le n} f(kd)|$ is unbounded for every $f:\mathbb N\to\{\pm1\}$; Tao proved it in 2015.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #178
research_problems.statement:
Let $A_1,A_2,\ldots$ be an infinite collection of infinite sets of integers, say
$A_i=\{a_{i1}<a_{i2}<\cdots\}$. Does there exist some $f:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\max_{m, 1\leq i\leq d} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq m} f(a_{ij})\right\rvert \ll_d 1$$
for all $d\geq 1$?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #1028
research_problems.statement:
Let
$$H(n)=\min_f \max_{X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}} \left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert,$$
where $f$ ranges over all functions $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\to \{-1,1\}$. Estimate $H(n)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #997
research_problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every $\alpha$, the sequence $\{ \alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed,
if $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #161
research_problems.statement:
(a) Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

(b) For fixed $t\geq 3$, do all positive densities below $1/2$ give the same asymptotic order?

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #162
research_problems.statement:
Let $\alpha > 0$ and $n \geq 1$. Let $F(n,\alpha)$ be the largest $k$ such that there exists some
2-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ in which any induced subgraph $H$ on at least $k$ vertices
contains more than $\alpha\binom{|H|}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #987
research_problems.statement:
For an infinite sequence $x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$, define
$$A_k = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \left\lvert \sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j) \right\rvert,$$
where $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$.

(a) Question 1:

Is it true that $\limsup_{k \to \infty} A_k = \infty$?

(b) **Question 2 (parts.ii)**: Is it possible for $A_k = o(k)$? Yes — there exists a sequence
$(x_n) \in (0, 1)$ and a bound $b(k) = o(k)$ with $A x k \le b k$ eventually. A corollary of
`sqrt_log_upper_bound` (which gives a $\sqrt{k \log k}$ bound) plus the asymptotic
$\sqrt{k \log k} = o(k)$.

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #995
research_problems.statement:
Erdős Problem 995:

For every lacunary sequence $(n_k)$ of integers and every $f \in L^2([0,1])$ with
$\int_0^1 f = 0$, is it true that for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\sum_{k < N} f(\{\alpha n_k\}) = o\!\left(N \sqrt{\log\log N}\right)?$$

research_problems.title: Erdős Problem #994
research_problems.statement:
Let $E\subseteq (0,1)$ be a meaurable subset with Lebesgue measure $\lambda(E)$. Is it true that,
for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}1_{\{k\alpha \}\in E}=\lambda(E)$$
for all $E$?
